| [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 | Promotion is audited in small persisted batches, ranked by expected yield, with decisions recorded apart from status changes | The owner's procedure of 2026-10-19 for finding entries whose evidence has outgrown their status. Candidates are triaged from metadata by a rubric that sets review order and never standing. They are reviewed five at a time, and each review ends in one of six dispositions with a specific blocker. Every step is persisted in record/promotion-audit/: a versioned queue.yaml with a hand-off block, one decision file per candidate, and one file per batch. A check keeps the queue and the decision files in step. Status changes go in separate pull requests of at most three entries. Rejected: one large audit held in a conversation, which is lost when the session is; a queue derived only from the decision files, which cannot say what is in progress; and promoting in the same step as reviewing. | Superseded — by [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md); Superseded on 2026-10-27 by the owner's acceptance of [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md), which derives the worklist from the record on each pass instead of keeping a queue. The three evidence rulings of versions 2 to 4 stand under it. |
| [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) v2 | A QUESTION is Answered by an Active CLAIM or THEORY, and a partly answered question is split into an Answered child and a narrowed Open parent | An Active THEORY is the record's current account, so it can answer a QUESTION as an Active CLAIM can. A CLAIM is not filed only to restate what a reading already establishes. A question is Answered when its Active answerers, alone or together, answer it as posed and in its full scope. When they answer only part of it, the answered part is filed as a child QUESTION that refines the parent and is marked Answered. The parent is reworded to what is left and stays Open. Rejected: requiring an Active CLAIM, which makes the record assert in its own voice what it relies on others to justify; marking a partly answered question Answered; and reframing the parent into new questions. | Active |
| [ADR-051](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-051.md) | A CASE names where the record got it: `reported_in` links it to the work, reading or account that reports it | A documented CASE usually comes from somewhere: a paper that reports a study, a reading that describes an episode, an account whose result the case records. The record had no field for that. A CASE could support a CLAIM but not point to a LIT, NOTE or THEORY, so its provenance lived in prose. At the owner's direction (2026-10-23), CASE gains `reported_in`, naming LITs, NOTEs and THEORYs, with the converse `reports` on each. It records provenance, not support. | Active |
| [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) v8 | Status review is ranked by reliance, derived from the record each pass, covers relations as well as statuses, and changes status in the pull request that decides it | The owner, 2026-10-27, after asking for status changes and relation changes on claims "that a lot of interesting downstream material depends on": the record had changed materially since the promotion audit of [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) stopped, and its process would benefit from changing. The audit never reached those claims: 15 of the 19 most-relied-on Proposed entries never entered its queue, its decision files went stale (230 of 308), and its owner questions sat unasked in a hand-off string. This decision replaces the procedure. A worklist is derived from the record's frontmatter on each pass and kept nowhere. It ranks Proposed entries by how much rests on them, and it lists credence inversions, retired premises and Open questions with an Active answer. A pass reviews a load-bearing entry together with the premises and objections that hold it back. It changes statuses and relations in its own pull request, records its reasoning on the entries and in one workbench entry, and puts its owner rulings in the pull request as a checklist. [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s three evidence rulings stand. Rejected: resuming the old queue, which would re-rank a record a third larger by a rubric that ranked these claims last; keeping per-code decision files, which drift from the entries they judge; and separate promotion pull requests, which took about 140 pull requests over three days and left five decided promotions undone. | Active |
| [ADR-107](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-107.md) v2 | An ARG may conclude a TERM, as an explication: that the definition does its declared job better than its predecessor and rivals, judged by Carnap's adequacy conditions; the verdict is the argument's and adoption stays the term's status, and the term's `argued_by` is derived | A TERM could reach upstream only to readings (`draws_on`, [ADR-095](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-095.md)) and to a broader term (`refines`, [ADR-046](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-046.md)). The claims and cases that fixed where a definition draws its lines were cited in its prose and nowhere else, so revising one of them found nothing built on it. The owner asked on 2026-11-19, after the definition of learning ([TERM-131](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-131.md)) took most of the exchange "Topological protection explained" to reach, whether TERMs should conclude ARGs. They now may, in one new form, `explication`, whose critical questions are Carnap's adequacy conditions (similarity to the paradigm cases, exactness, fruitfulness, simplicity) and the rivals it is judged against. Its verdict is on fit to the term's job ([ADR-056](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-056.md)), not on truth, which is [CLAIM-472](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-472.md)'s point that a cut is open to evaluation and not only to verification. The term's `argued_by` is derived. Rejected: a twin adequacy CLAIM for each term; widening `draws_on` to claims and cases; leaving it to prose. | Active |
| [ADR-141](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-141.md) | Every long-running or delegated unit of work persists its progress in the repository as it goes, on a branch of its own, so that a stop at any moment loses at most the step in hand | Alternative (a) of two, filed on the owner's request of 2026-11-22 to stop losing work and to consider which decision needs superseding. [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) makes delegated readers push running notes as they read, but it covers readers only. On 2026-11-22 work was lost or put at risk three ways it does not reach: a lead worker's brief said to commit at the end; the assistant's own background sweep of 184 Unfetched works held its results in memory and was stopped at 162 by the time limit, losing the probe details; and the briefs and triage tables lived in the session's scratchpad, which dies with the container. A devlog note of the same morning had already drawn the lesson for filers and nothing carried it out. Decided, superseding [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) and keeping its reader rules: every unit of work that runs past one tool call, delegated or the assistant's own, works on a branch of its own from its first minute; pushes after every step; keeps a PROGRESS file a replacement can resume from; writes computed results per item, append-only and resumable, inside the repository, with checkpoint commits; is given a time limit above twice its estimate and is restructured, not left to run, when its pace says it will not finish; and keeps briefs and working tables in the repository rather than the scratchpad. The measure is that a stop at any moment loses at most the step in hand. The first application is the lead-worker brief moved into the repository as the run-lead skill. The alternative is [ADR-142](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-142.md), which leaves [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) standing. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [ADR-142](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-142.md) | Lead workers and long computations persist their progress as they go, as delegated readers already do, on a branch of their own, so that a stop loses at most the step in hand | Alternative (b) of two, filed on the owner's request of 2026-11-22 to stop losing work. It leaves [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) standing for readers and adds the two kinds of work that lost or risked work that day: lead workers, whose brief said to commit at the end, and long computations, whose results were held in memory until the end. Each pushes after every step from a branch of its own; a computation writes each item's result as it is produced, inside the repository, resumes by skipping what is written, and is checkpointed at least every ten minutes; a background run gets a time limit above twice its estimate and is restructured when its pace says it will not finish; the lead-worker brief moves into the repository as a skill. The alternative is [ADR-141](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-141.md), which supersedes [ADR-108](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-108.md) with one general rule. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
